I wanted to give this plain front yard a premium upgrade, so I grabbed my tools and got to work! Watching the real progress unfold in this timelapse is incredibly satisfying. Here is a step-by-step breakdown of how I built this modern rock garden: 1️⃣ First, I mapped out a smooth, curved border on the grass using white spray paint. 2️⃣ Next, I dug out the edge along the line and laid down a heavy-duty black weed barrier. 3️⃣ I installed a sleek stone border, block by block, to keep everything neat and contained. 4️⃣ Then came the best part—pouring and leveling tons of crisp white river rocks for that beautiful, high-contrast look. 5️⃣ Finally, I styled the space by placing a dark statement sphere, planting some architectural agaves, and adding solar pathway lights. Seeing the before and after of this build progress makes all the hard work totally worth it! Let me know what you think of the final result in the comments, and don't forget to follow Dust to Dreamy for more ideas. 👇 #BuildProgress #BeforeAndAfter #YardMakeover #Landscaping #DIYProject

I was called in to replace the fence panels and totally rip out the garden  (not the posts, they are a bit crooked but they are still standing😅)  I started with the fence panels, then began to totally clear the area of weeds and any other debris in the garden. ✨ Want a stunning, weed-free flower bed? Try this easy "pot-in-pot" landscaping hack to keep your borders looking fresh all year long! 📦 First, lay down cardboard along your path and space out heavy-duty black base pots on top. The cardboard acts as an amazing, natural weed barrier. 💧 Next, pour gravel all around the base pots. This hides the cardboard, holds your base pots securely in place, and provides excellent water drainage. 🪴 Now just drop your decorative plants-still in their own nursery pots-directly into the base pots! You can swap them out in seconds when seasons change or easily lift them inside if a freeze hits. 💡 Pro-tips: Mix up your flower colors, put the taller plants in the back, and always match your plants to the amount of sunlight that wall gets.

⚠️ To everyone in the 559 area, please be cautious when hiring Premier Landscape. Unfortunately, our experience with this contractor has been extremely disappointing. We had such high expectations, especially considering this was a $140,000 backyard project. Throughout the entire process, we made every single payment on time. Not once did we delay a payment. If anything, we were extremely patient and understanding with the constant delays, many of which were not related to city inspections but rather the contractor’s inability to get the work completed as scheduled. Fast-forward to today, and we’re still left with unfinished work, an incomplete waterfall, concrete with significant issues, and a pool that has STILL not passed its final inspection. What’s even more frustrating is the lack of communication. Our calls and messages have gone unanswered, and we’ve now discovered that the contractor has blocked us on social media. At this point, we’re genuinely concerned that he has no intention of returning to finish our project. It’s extremely upsetting because we worked hard to afford this backyard, trusted this company with our home, and held up our end of the agreement every step of the way. We paid for a completed $140,000 project, and that’s not what we’ve received. I’m sharing our personal experience because I wouldn’t want another family to go through the same frustration, stress, and disappointment we’ve experienced.
